title: Textures & an Asset Browser
summary: Show OpenGL textures with Image/ImageButton, use UVs for tiling, flipping and zoom, build a wrapping thumbnail browser with tooltips and drag-to-apply, and generate textures at runtime.

quiz.q: With the OpenGL backend, what is an ImTextureID?
options: The GLuint texture name, cast to ImTextureID
An index into ImGui's font atlas
quiz.explain: ImGui stores the ID and hands it back to the backend, which calls glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, (GLuint)(intptr_t)id).

quiz.q: Which UVs show a texture flipped vertically?
quiz.explain: Swapping the V coordinates flips vertically. This is what you need when showing an FBO render target.

quiz.q: Why does ImageButton take a string as its first argument?
options: It's the ID, since several buttons may show the same texture
quiz.explain: The ID used to come from the texture itself, which broke when two buttons shared a texture. Now you pass an explicit ID (usually "##thumb" inside PushID(i)).
